Applying this lemma to f (x) = xn + axn-1 + pq with p as a prime, if f (x) is reducible, it must have a rational root. Since f (x) is monic with integer coefficients, this rational root must be an integer. 3. Let r be an integer root of f (x). Then: rn + arn-1 + pq = 0 =⇒ pq = -rn - arn-1. Since pq is squarefree, r must be ±1. 4. If r = 1: 1n + a · 1n-1 + pq = 0 =⇒ 1 + a + pq = 0 =⇒ a = -1 - pq. 5.
